messages:
june: Incoming from BrightAxis (org_id: org_BA42). They hit a hard 429 at 2026-02-14T16:12Z during a customer-facing demo. Customer says "requests are failing sporadically" and wants an immediate fix. Pls triage.

diego: Can you grab one of their x-request-id values and full response headers? Also want the org's plan and whether they recently changed any client code.

june: They pasted a response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 500/min
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1718409178
Retry-After: 60
x-request-id: rq_7f9d1c2e
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded: burst quota","type":"rate_limit"}}
```
Times: 2026-02-14T16:12:02Z, 16:12:18Z, 16:12:47Z. Client IPs: 18.204.11.7 and 18.204.11.8. They attached an SDK snippet showing concurrent loop fire-and-forget.

billing-bot: Automated note: Account plan = Free Trial (trial credits). Trial per-minute default = 60 req/min but we have a promotional soft-burst allowance up to 500/min for short-lived demos; monthly token credit remaining = 5,200 tokens. Billing contact on file = acct_ops@brightaxis.io.

lia: Hmm — two things: 1) Their client is launching ~8 parallel requests with max_tokens=2000 and big system prompts; tokens per request likely >2k. 2) We throttle by both request/min and token windows; bursts from IPs can hit our global anti-abuse guard which surfaces as "burst quota" 429s. If they hit token budget quickly that explains errors.

june: Customer insists they only sent 10 requests in 2 minutes. They ran a stress script; our logs show repeated request groups with same user-agent and many overlapping x-request-ids in that minute. Could be a retry storm or misconfigured client.

diego: I opened SUP-8932 and attached logs. I'm proposing two immediate actions: (A) temporary demo exception: lift their per-minute request cap to 500/min for 24 hours scoped to org_BA42 and IP range, and (B) a protective rule: limit concurrent in-flight requests per API key to 6 to prevent client retry storms. Ops - can you apply A and B?

ops-bot: Request received. Note: applying soft policy requires sales sign-off for >2 hours. Request queued.

sales-ryan: I can approve a 24-hour demo bump to 500/min with a note to billing. I'll email acct_ops@brightaxis.io to confirm acceptance of demo terms (no charge, auto-revert). If they need sustained >500/min we'll convert to Starter tier and discuss pro-rated billing. Ryan will log in CRM.

lia: Tech suggestion for the customer message to send: ask them to reduce max_tokens from 2000 to 512, switch on streaming, and add client-side leaky-bucket rate limiter set to 8 req/min with jittered backoff. Also share a snippet they can drop-in: 
```js
// client-side leaky bucket (pseudo)
const limiter = new LeakyBucket({capacity:8, refillRatePerSec:0.5});
await limiter.removeToken();
await client.generate({...});
```
This will cut accidental bursts and perceived latency.

june: I sent the customer step-by-step: reduce max_tokens, enable streaming, and confirm no automated retries higher than 3 attempts with exponential backoff. I also told them we're provisioning a 24h bump pending their confirmation on the billing email. They replied "confirm, please enable asap".

ops-bot: Temporary policy applied by diego at 2026-02-14T16:25:12Z: org_BA42 allowed up to 500 req/min from 2026-02-14T16:26Z to 2026-02-15T16:26Z. Concurrent in-flight cap = 6 applied to their API key. Auto-rollback scheduled.

billing-bot: Billing note: trial account - no charge for 24h demo bump. If upgraded to Starter within 7 days, pro-rated invoice will be generated. Billing contact notified via email.

sales-ryan: I'll follow up with a short Starter plan quote: 2k req/min, token commitment option, and 30-day onboarding call. If they accept, we can remove the concurrent cap and set higher per-route quotas.

customer-bot: BrightAxis: Thanks, team. Demo resumed. We'll trim prompt sizes and enable streaming. Please confirm we'll revert to previous limits automatically.

june: Confirmed with ops-bot and closed high priority escalation. Posting remediation checklist to customer: 1) reduce prompt size / max_tokens, 2) enable streaming, 3) add client-side limiter + jitter, 4) if long-term >500/min needs Starter plan, contact sales.

lia: Follow-up engineering note: we should ask product to document demo exception process publicly to speed future handling and reduce backlog. Also recommend a new SDK helper that exposes a client-rate-limiter out of the box.

diego: SUP-8932 status: resolved (temporary bump applied). Will convert to follow-up ticket for sales handoff.

ops-bot: Rollback scheduled at 2026-02-15T16:26:00Z.
